# Pattern Review: Brackenford Hall

## Input Quality and Limitations

The log contains two reports covering one event, A, in room 1 on day 2. E1 and E2 are separate occurrences but refer to the same underlying instance. The technician reproduced the failure and confirmed a damaged cable; replacement removed the fault. No diagnostic gap is apparent for this instance.

## Summary

| Candidate | Occurrences | Distinct Instances | Cause Consistency | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Projector cutting out due to a damaged cable | 2 | 1 | Both reports concern the same confirmed failure | High for this isolated diagnosis; no repeated-instance pattern established |

## Genuine Patterns

None. There are not two distinct instances supporting a recurring cause.

## Misleading Surface Patterns

E1 and E2 repeat the exact wording, “The projector cuts out.” This is repeated reporting of one failure, not evidence of multiple failures. No different-cause surface pattern is shown.

## Isolated Signals, Not Yet Patterns

E1 and E2 support one damaged-cable incident. Reproduction and successful cable replacement provide strong evidence for the diagnosis. The limiting evidence is that both reports concern event A: two attendees do not establish recurrence across events.

## Suggested Actions for Human Approval

A person should review the diagnosis and decide whether any further action is warranted. The cable replacement is already recorded as completed; this log alone does not establish a need for a broader maintenance or process change.

## What This Sample Cannot Tell You

It cannot establish recurrence across events, rooms or days, a failure rate, or a wider cable-quality problem. What recurs is the report wording, not an independently repeated fault.
